small_guidance:
- The conv dominates runtime here (B=1024, C=16, D=16, H=W=32 with kernel 4 — output is ~13×29×29×1024×16 ≈ huge). The post-conv fused kernel is already cheap; further tuning of BLOCK_S/num_warps will not move the needle. If staying small, narrow the autotune list to BLOCK_S∈{2048,4096}, num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages=2 to reduce autotune overhead.
- Consider folding the conv bias add into the fused kernel by skipping bias in `self.conv` and loading bias inside the kernel — but the real cost is the conv itself.
- Keep `x_flat` in (B, C, S) layout already contiguous; no further layout gain inside the existing kernel.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: with in_channels=3, kernel=4 → K = 3·4·4·4 = 192, OC=16, output spatial = 13·29·29 = 10933, B=1024. One program per (B, OC tile, output-spatial tile); BLOCK_M=16 (OC), BLOCK_N=64–128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=192 (fits in one step). Fuse HardSwish in the epilogue and write the result directly into the per-(B,C,S) buffer consumed by the GroupNorm-mean kernel.
- Better: fuse Conv3D + HardSwish + GroupNorm-mean into one persistent kernel per (B, group). Each program computes its group's conv outputs on the fly (looping over output spatial positions, accumulating partial conv via small inner-product), applies HardSwish, and accumulates ch_sum / sum / sumsq in registers — eliminating the conv output materialization (~5 GB) entirely.
- If full fusion is too complex, at minimum write the conv as a Triton kernel in NHWC/channels-last-3d layout so the K=192 reduction is contiguous; the current torch Conv3d on this tiny-channel shape is bandwidth-bound and has lots of headroom.
